islands.name: Head and Neck
islands.intro: Master 28 facial, mastication, and neck muscles & nerves.
points: Grouping 1 - Superficial Facial Expression (CN VII Facial nerve): Orbicularis oculi (closes eyelids), Orbicularis oris (compresses/protrudes lips), Nasalis (opens/closes nostrils), Buccinator (builds cheek structure, controls food)

Grouping 2 - Deep Mastication (CN V Trigeminal nerve): Temporalis (elevates/retracts mandible), Masseter (elevates/protrudes mandible from zygomatic arch), Lateral pterygoid (protrudes/depresses mandible, contralateral deviation), Medial pterygoid (elevates/protrudes mandible, contralateral deviation)

Grouping 3 - Superficial, Suprahyoid & Infrahyoid Neck: Platysma (CN VII), Sternocleidomastoid (manubrium/clavicle to mastoid process, CN XI, contralateral rotation & ipsilateral lateral flexion), Digastric/Mylohyoid/Geniohyoid/Stylohyoid (elevate hyoid & depress mandible), Omohyoid/Sternothyroid/Thyrohyoid (depress/stabilize hyoid & larynx via Ansa cervicalis & C1)

Grouping 4 - Deep Prevertebral, Scalenes & Suboccipital: Longus capitis/Longus colli/Rectus capitis anterior & lateralis (head/neck flexion), Scalene anterior/medius/posterior (C2-C7 TP to 1st/2nd ribs, elevate ribs & ipsilateral neck flexion), Rectus capitis posterior major/minor & Obliquus capitis inferior/superior (C1-C2 to occiput, Suboccipital nerve, head extension & ipsilateral rotation)

RPG Quiz Directives: Generate English multiple-choice and dialogue battles testing exact Muscle Origin, Insertion, Muscle Action (unilateral vs bilateral), and Cranial/Spinal Nerve Innervation from Head and Neck CSV & 3D images
islands.extra: Accurately identify the Origin, Insertion, Unilateral vs. Bilateral Action, and Cranial/Cervical Nerve Innervation of all 28 Head and Neck muscles through RPG monster quizzes.
materials: materials/01_Head and Neck/Head and Neck - 3D Muscle Atlas Reference.docx
materials/01_Head and Neck/Physiotherapy Anatomy Muscle Database - Head and Neck.csv

islands.name: Shoulder
islands.intro: Conquer 17 pectoral, rotator cuff, and scapular muscles.
points: Grouping 1 - Pectoral Region: Pectoralis major (clavicular & sternocostal heads to lateral lip of bicipital groove, adducts/medially rotates/flexes humerus, Lateral & medial pectoral nerves), Pectoralis minor (ribs 3-5 to coracoid process, protracts/depresses scapula), Serratus anterior (ribs 1-9 to medial border of scapula, protracts/upwardly rotates scapula, Long thoracic nerve), Subclavius (1st rib to clavicle, Subclavian nerve)

Grouping 2 - Rotator Cuff (SITS): Supraspinatus (supraspinous fossa to greater tubercle, abducts humerus, Suprascapular nerve), Infraspinatus (infraspinous fossa to greater tubercle, lateral rotation, Suprascapular nerve), Teres minor (lateral border of scapula to greater tubercle, lateral rotation, Axillary nerve), Subscapularis (subscapular fossa to lesser tubercle, medial rotation, Upper & lower subscapular nerves)

Grouping 3 - Glenohumeral: Deltoid (clavicle/acromion/spine of scapula to deltoid tuberosity, flexion/abduction/extension of humerus, Axillary nerve), Teres major (inferior angle of scapula to medial lip of bicipital groove, adducts/extends/medially rotates humerus, Lower subscapular nerve)

Grouping 4 - Superficial Back & Shoulder Girdle: Trapezius Upper/Middle/Lower fibers (occiput/C7-T12 to clavicle/acromion/scapular spine, elevation/retraction/depression/upward rotation, CN XI Accessory nerve), Latissimus dorsi (T7-T12/iliac crest/ribs 9-12 to floor of bicipital groove, Thoracodorsal nerve), Rhomboid minor & major (C7-T5 to medial border of scapula, retraction & downward rotation, Dorsal scapular nerve), Levator scapulae (C1-C4 TP to superior angle of scapula, elevates/downwardly rotates scapula)

RPG Quiz Directives: Test players on distinguishing Rotator Cuff vs. Scapular Stabilizer origins, insertions (greater vs. lesser tubercle vs. intertubercular sulcus), actions, and brachial plexus nerves in English
islands.extra: Differentiate the Origin, Insertion, Scapular vs. Glenohumeral Action, and Innervation of all 17 Shoulder and Rotator Cuff muscles in English quiz battles.

islands.name: Elbow
islands.intro: Explore 9 arm and forearm flexors, extensors & rotators.
points: Grouping 1 - Anterior Arm (Musculocutaneous nerve): Coracobrachialis (coracoid process to middle 1/3 medial humerus, flexes/adducts humerus), Biceps brachii (short head: coracoid apex
long head: supraglenoid tubercle to radial tuberosity, flexes & supinates forearm), Brachialis (distal 1/2 anterior humerus to ulnar coronoid process/tuberosity, flexes elbow in all positions)
Grouping 2 - Posterior Arm & Elbow (Radial nerve): Triceps brachii (long head: infraglenoid tubercle

lateral & medial heads: posterior humerus to olecranon of ulna, extends elbow & long head extends/adducts humerus), Anconeus (lateral epicondyle to olecranon, extends elbow), Brachioradialis (lateral supracondylar ridge to distal radius, flexes elbow)

Grouping 3 - Radioulnar Pronators (Median / Anterior interosseous nerve): Pronator teres (medial epicondyle & ulnar coronoid process to middle 1/3 lateral radius, pronates & flexes forearm), Pronator quadratus (distal 1/4 anterior ulna to distal 1/4 anterior radius, pronates forearm)

Grouping 4 - Radioulnar Supinator: Supinator (lateral epicondyle, radial collateral/annular ligaments & supinator crest of ulna to proximal 1/3 radius, supinates forearm, Posterior interosseous nerve)
RPG Quiz Directives: Create English quiz questions comparing elbow flexors across forearm positions, two-joint vs. one-joint muscles, and Musculocutaneous vs. Radial vs. Median nerve supply
islands.extra: Master the exact Origin, Insertion, Elbow/Radioulnar Action, and Innervation of all 9 Elbow and Forearm rotation muscles through interactive challenges.

islands.name: Wrist and Hands
islands.intro: Test 27 forearm and intrinsic hand muscles & nerve supply.
points: Grouping 1 - Anterior Forearm Flexors: Flexor carpi radialis, Palmaris longus, Flexor digitorum superficialis (Median nerve), Flexor carpi ulnaris (Ulnar nerve), Flexor digitorum profundus (Medial 1/2 Ulnar nerve
Lateral 1/2 Anterior interosseous nerve to distal phalanges #2-5), Flexor pollicis longus (Anterior interosseous nerve to thumb distal phalanx)

Grouping 2 - Posterior Forearm Extensors (Radial / Posterior interosseous nerve): Extensor carpi radialis longus & brevis, Extensor carpi ulnaris, Extensor digitorum, Extensor digiti minimi, Abductor pollicis longus, Extensor pollicis longus & brevis, Extensor indicis

Grouping 3 - Intrinsic Hand Thenar & Hypothenar: Abductor pollicis brevis, Flexor pollicis brevis, Opponens pollicis (Recurrent branch of median nerve), Abductor digiti minimi, Flexor digiti minimi brevis, Opponens digiti minimi (Deep branch of ulnar nerve)

Grouping 4 - Intrinsic Short Palmar & Dorsal: Lumbricals #1+2 (Median nerve) & #3+4 (Deep ulnar nerve, flex MCP & extend IP joints from FDP tendons), Palmar interossei #1-3 (adduct fingers PAD, Deep ulnar nerve), Dorsal interossei #1-4 (abduct fingers DAB, Deep ulnar nerve), Adductor pollicis (Deep ulnar nerve), Palmaris brevis (Superficial ulnar nerve)

RPG Quiz Directives: Quiz players in English on common flexor/extensor tendon origins, PIP vs. DIP insertions (FDS vs. FDP), anatomical snuffbox tendons, and Median vs. Ulnar vs. Radial nerve territories
islands.extra: Identify the Origin, Insertion, Digit/Wrist Action, and Median, Ulnar, or Radial Nerve Innervation for all 27 Wrist and Hand muscles.
materials: materials/04_Wrist and Hands/Wrist and Hands - 3D Muscle Atlas Reference.docx
materials/04_Wrist and Hands/Physiotherapy Anatomy Muscle Database - Wrist and Hands.csv

islands.name: Trunk
islands.intro: Challenge 26 back, abdominal, respiratory & pelvic muscles.
points: Grouping 1 - Extrinsic & Intrinsic Back: Serratus posterior superior (elevates ribs 2-5) & inferior (depresses ribs 9-12), Splenius capitis & cervicis, Erector spinae (Iliocostalis, Longissimus, Spinalis), Semispinalis, Multifidus, Interspinales, Intertransversarii, Rotatores, Levatores costarum (Posterior rami of spinal nerves, spinal extension, stabilization, ipsilateral lateral flexion & contralateral/ipsilateral rotation)

Grouping 2 - Anterior & Posterior Abdominal Wall: External obliques (ribs 5-12 to linea alba/iliac crest, contralateral rotation), Internal obliques (ipsilateral rotation), Rectus abdominis (pubis to xiphoid/ribs 5-7, trunk flexion), Transversus abdominis (intra-abdominal pressure), Quadratus lumborum (iliac crest to 12th rib/L1-L4 TP, ipsilateral lateral flexion & hip hiking), Psoas minor
Grouping 3 - Thoracic Respiratory: Diaphragm (xiphoid, lower 6 ribs & lumbar vertebrae to central tendon, primary inspiration, Phrenic nerve)

Grouping 4 - Pelvic Floor & Perineum: Levator ani (Puborectalis, Pubococcygeus, Iliococcygeus) & Coccygeus (pelvic floor elevation & visceral support), External anal sphincter, Superficial & Deep transverse perinei, Ischiocavernosus, Bulbospongiosus (Perineal & inferior rectal nerves)
RPG Quiz Directives: Test players in English on ipsilateral vs. contralateral trunk rotators, deep spinal stabilizers, Diaphragm attachments, and Pelvic Floor actions
islands.extra: Master the Origin, Insertion, Unilateral vs. Bilateral Action, and Innervation of all 26 Back, Abdominal, Respiratory, and Pelvic Floor muscles.

islands.name: Hip
islands.intro: Master 17 gluteal, iliopsoas, rotator & adductor muscles.
points: Grouping 1 - Anterior Hip / Iliopsoas: Iliacus (iliac fossa/sacral ala to lesser trochanter, Femoral nerve) & Psoas major (T12-L5 to lesser trochanter, Lumbar anterior rami, hip flexion & external rotation)

Grouping 2 - Gluteal Region: Gluteus maximus (posterior ilium/sacrum to IT tract & gluteal tuberosity, hip extension & lateral rotation, Inferior gluteal nerve), Gluteus medius & Gluteus minimus (ilium to greater trochanter, hip abduction & medial rotation, keeps pelvis level, Superior gluteal nerve), Tensor fasciae latae (ASIS/iliac crest to IT tract, Superior gluteal nerve)

Grouping 3 - Deep External Rotators: Piriformis, Obturator internus, Superior gemellus, Inferior gemellus, Quadratus femoris (sacrum/ischium/obturator margin to greater trochanter/quadrate tubercle, lateral rotation when extended & abduction when flexed)

Grouping 4 - Medial Thigh Adductors: Pectineus (Femoral/Obturator nerve), Adductor longus, Adductor brevis, Gracilis (pes anserinus), Obturator externus (Obturator nerve), Adductor magnus (Adductor part: ischiopubic ramus to linea aspera, Obturator nerve
Hamstring part: ischial tuberosity to adductor tubercle, Tibial nerve)
RPG Quiz Directives: Generate English battle questions on Superior vs. Inferior gluteal nerve, dual innervation of Adductor magnus, and deep external rotator attachments
islands.extra: Accurately recall the Origin, Insertion, Pelvic/Femoral Action, and Nerve Supply for all 17 Hip and Medial Thigh muscles.

islands.name: Knee
islands.intro: Conquer 9 quadriceps, hamstring, and popliteal muscles.
points: Grouping 1 - Anterior Thigh Quadriceps & Sartorius (Femoral nerve): Rectus femoris (AIIS & superior acetabulum to tibial tuberosity via patellar tendon, flexes hip & extends knee), Vastus medialis (intertrochanteric line/medial linea aspera), Vastus intermedius (anterior/lateral femur), Vastus lateralis (greater trochanter/lateral linea aspera, all extend knee), Sartorius (ASIS to pes anserinus on medial proximal tibia, flexes/abducts/laterally rotates hip & flexes/medially rotates knee)

Grouping 2 - Posterior Thigh Hamstrings: Semitendinosus (ischial tuberosity to pes anserinus, extends hip, flexes & medially rotates knee, Tibial division of sciatic nerve), Semimembranosus (ischial tuberosity to medial tibial condyle, extends hip, flexes & medially rotates knee, Tibial division), Biceps femoris (Long head: ischial tuberosity, Tibial division
Short head: lateral linea aspera, Common fibular division
inserts on fibular head, flexes & laterally rotates knee)
Grouping 3 - Posterior Knee: Popliteus (lateral femoral condyle to posterior tibia above soleal line, unlocks knee via lateral rotation of femur on fixed tibia, Tibial nerve)

RPG Quiz Directives: Test players in English on Pes Anserinus insertions (Sartorius, Gracilis, Semitendinosus), biarticular vs. monoarticular quadriceps/hamstrings, and Popliteus knee-unlocking mechanics
islands.extra: Master the Origin, Insertion, Biarticular Action, and Sciatic/Femoral/Tibial Innervation of all 9 Knee and Thigh muscles.

islands.name: Ankle and Foot
islands.intro: Explore 24 crural compartments and intrinsic foot muscles.
points: Grouping 1 - Anterior & Lateral Leg: Tibialis anterior (dorsiflexion & inversion), Extensor hallucis longus, Extensor digitorum longus, Fibularis tertius (dorsiflexion & eversion, all Deep fibular nerve), Fibularis longus & Fibularis brevis (plantarflexion & eversion, Superficial fibular nerve)

Grouping 2 - Superficial & Deep Posterior Leg (Tibial nerve): Gastrocnemius, Soleus, Plantaris (insert on calcaneus via calcaneal tendon, plantarflexion), Tibialis posterior (plantarflexion & inversion, arch support), Flexor digitorum longus, Flexor hallucis longus
Grouping 3 - Dorsal Foot (Deep fibular nerve): Extensor digitorum brevis, Extensor hallucis brevis

Grouping 4 - Intrinsic Sole of Foot (Layers 1-4): Layer 1 - Abductor hallucis & Flexor digitorum brevis (Medial plantar nerve), Abductor digiti minimi (Lateral plantar nerve), Layer 2 - Quadratus plantae (Lateral plantar nerve) & Lumbricals #1-4 (#1 Medial plantar, #2-4 Lateral plantar), Layer 3 - Flexor hallucis brevis (Medial plantar), Adductor hallucis & Flexor digiti minimi brevis (Lateral plantar), Layer 4 - Plantar interossei #1-3 (adduct digits 3-5) & Dorsal interossei #1-4 (abduct digits 2-4, Lateral plantar nerve)
RPG Quiz Directives: Challenge players in English on ankle dorsiflexors vs. plantarflexors, invertors vs. evertors, plantar foot layers 1-4, and Medial vs. Lateral plantar nerve supply
islands.extra: Differentiate the Origin, Insertion, Compartment/Layer Action, and Fibular/Tibial/Plantar Innervation of all 24 Ankle and Foot muscles.
materials: materials/08_Ankle and Foot/Physiotherapy Anatomy Muscle Database - Ankle and Foot.csv
materials/08_Ankle and Foot/Ankle and Foot - 3D Muscle Atlas Reference.docx

detail.name: 極致
detail.requirement: 在精緻之上：每島至少 1 個會動的小機關（風車、水車、旗子、噴泉）、地面有色塊拼貼與陰影細節、島底岩層分層；需提供「低畫質」切換並在手機自動降級

cinema.name: 電影史詩
cinema.requirement: 開場 4～6 秒：從遠方高空穿過雲層、環繞群島半圈、俯衝拉近再拉遠成全景（可加輕微景深模糊與標題淡入）；點島時鏡頭先拉高、沿弧線繞到島的正面再推近（1.5～2.5 秒）；任何時候點畫面或按 Esc 可以跳過
